title: Hybrid & Advanced Networking
oneLiner: Connect on-premises to AWS and wire many VPCs together: Direct Connect, VPN, Transit Gateway, and peering.
examWeightNote: Hybrid connectivity shows up across Resilient and High-Performing architecture questions.
objectives: Contrast Site-to-Site VPN with AWS Direct Connect on cost, speed, and consistency.
Use Transit Gateway to connect many VPCs and on-prem networks at scale.
Know when to use VPC peering vs Transit Gateway, and that peering is non-transitive.
Reach AWS services privately with VPC endpoints and PrivateLink.

services.name: AWS Direct Connect
services.purpose: A dedicated private physical link from your data center to AWS — consistent low latency and bandwidth.

services.name: Site-to-Site VPN
services.purpose: Encrypted IPsec tunnels over the public internet between on-prem and a VPC — quick to set up.

services.name: AWS Transit Gateway
services.purpose: A cloud router hub connecting thousands of VPCs and on-prem networks through one attachment each.

services.name: VPC Peering
services.purpose: A one-to-one private connection between two VPCs; simple but non-transitive.

services.name: PrivateLink / VPC Endpoints
services.purpose: Reach AWS or third-party services privately without traversing the internet.

keyConcepts: Site-to-Site VPN is fast to deploy and cheap but rides the public internet (variable latency); Direct Connect is a dedicated private link with consistent performance but takes weeks to provision and costs more.
For resilience, pair Direct Connect with a backup VPN, or use two Direct Connect connections.
Transit Gateway is a hub-and-spoke router: attach many VPCs and VPN/Direct Connect once, instead of a mesh of peerings.
VPC peering is non-transitive — if A peers with B and B peers with C, A still can't reach C. Transit Gateway solves this at scale.
A Direct Connect Gateway lets one Direct Connect reach VPCs in multiple Regions.
Use interface endpoints (PrivateLink) for most services and free gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB to keep traffic off the internet.

diagram.caption: On-prem connects to AWS via Direct Connect and/or VPN, then a Transit Gateway fans out to many VPCs.
diagram.note: VPC peering would need a connection between every pair (and isn't transitive); Transit Gateway needs just one attachment per network.

scenarios.scenario: A company has 25 VPCs that all need to communicate, plus connectivity to their on-prem network. A full mesh of VPC peering is becoming unmanageable.
scenarios.question: What should they use to simplify connectivity at scale?

options.label: AWS Transit Gateway as a central hub for all VPCs and the on-prem link
A NAT gateway in each VPC

scenarios.explanation: Transit Gateway replaces an N×N peering mesh with a hub: each VPC and the on-prem connection attach once. Peering is non-transitive and doesn't scale to many VPCs.

scenarios.scenario: A workload needs consistent, low-latency, high-bandwidth connectivity between on-prem and AWS for a latency-sensitive application, not best-effort internet.
scenarios.question: Which connectivity option best fits?

options.label: AWS Direct Connect (optionally with a VPN backup)

scenarios.explanation: Direct Connect provides a dedicated private link with consistent latency and bandwidth. A VPN rides the public internet with variable performance; add a VPN as a cheaper backup path for resilience.

quiz.question: A key difference between Site-to-Site VPN and Direct Connect is that Direct Connect:
options: Is a dedicated private link with consistent latency/bandwidth (but slower to provision)
quiz.answer: Is a dedicated private link with consistent latency/bandwidth (but slower to provision)
quiz.explanation: Direct Connect is a private physical connection with predictable performance; VPN is quick and cheap but uses the public internet with variable latency.

quiz.question: Why does VPC peering not scale well to many VPCs?
options: It is non-transitive and needs a connection between every pair of VPCs
It only works within one subnet
quiz.answer: It is non-transitive and needs a connection between every pair of VPCs
quiz.explanation: Peering is one-to-one and non-transitive, so connecting N VPCs needs an N×N mesh. Transit Gateway centralizes this.

quiz.question: What is AWS Transit Gateway best described as?
options: A central cloud router that connects many VPCs and on-prem networks via single attachments
quiz.answer: A central cloud router that connects many VPCs and on-prem networks via single attachments
quiz.explanation: Transit Gateway is hub-and-spoke routing — attach each VPC/VPN/Direct Connect once instead of meshing peerings.

quiz.question: To make a Direct Connect connection resilient at lower cost, a common pattern is to:
options: Add a Site-to-Site VPN as a backup path
Use a single connection and hope
quiz.answer: Add a Site-to-Site VPN as a backup path
quiz.explanation: A VPN backup provides a failover path if the Direct Connect link goes down; for higher resilience use redundant Direct Connect connections.

quiz.question: Which lets a single Direct Connect connection reach VPCs in multiple AWS Regions?
quiz.explanation: A Direct Connect Gateway associates a Direct Connect with VPCs (via gateways) across multiple Regions.

quiz.question: To privately access Amazon S3 from a VPC without any internet path, you would use:
quiz.explanation: S3 and DynamoDB use free gateway VPC endpoints; most other services use interface endpoints (PrivateLink).

quiz.question: A Site-to-Site VPN connection provides:
options: A plaintext link over a private line
Encrypted IPsec tunnels over the public internet
quiz.answer: Encrypted IPsec tunnels over the public internet
quiz.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN establishes encrypted IPsec tunnels between your on-prem gateway and AWS over the internet.
